The entire commercial portion of the Dairy Farm Guildford Road Shopping Centre will be sold via a public tender closing at noon on November 19, according to sole agent CBRE.

articles.title: Hong Kong outlines 4-step AI ‘talent ladder’ to offset entry-level job shock
articles.summary:
Hong Kong has unveiled a four-step artificial intelligence (AI) “talent ladder” strategy to counter entry-level job shock and foster industry leaders, viewing the technology as a “catalyst, not a threat”.
Permanent Secretary for Innovation, Technology and Industry Kevin Choi Kit-ming warned on Monday that the “entry-level shock” was real because AI performed well in many routine tasks that once made up a graduate’s first job, such as basic coding and first-line customer service.

articles.title: China develops plant to extract hydrogen, fresh water and uranium from the sea
articles.summary:
Chinese scientists have built a small, stable co-production plant that uses one system to extract hydrogen and fresh water from seawater, while also recovering uranium and bromine and improving electricity use efficiency by about 15 per cent.
The team, led by Deng Dehui and Liu Yanting from the Chinese Academy of Sciences’ Dalian Institute of Chemical Physics, improved on an existing technology that is both costly and power hungry, according to a paper in the peer-reviewed journal Nature...

articles.summary:
Hong Kong’s largest public hospital, built on the former airport site in Kai Tak, will begin its first phase of operation on Monday after more than a decade of planning and preparation.

articles.summary:
An elderly man in central China, who has spent the past 21 years making ends meet as a scavenger, experienced a remarkable stroke of luck when he discovered that his pension fund contained over 420,000 yuan (US$63,000).
In late September, the 71-year-old man, surnamed Ru, received a bank card linked to his pension account, which revealed a balance of 424,204 yuan, as reported by Changde Daily.

articles.summary:
Housewife May and her three children were overjoyed last September when they moved into a 200 sq ft subdivided flat in Kwai Tsing, a Hong Kong district with one of the city’s lowest average monthly household incomes.
For years, the 50-year-old single parent had lived in a squatter hut with her son and two daughters, where they had to climb hundreds of stairs daily. They later moved into a 100 sq ft subdivided flat before securing their current place.

articles.title: HKU eyes Northern Metropolis expansion to boost research capacity, attract talent
articles.summary:
The University of Hong Kong (HKU) is looking to secure more laboratory space in the Northern Metropolis university town to expand its research capacity and attract talent, its new vice-president for research has said.
Professor Anderson Shum Ho-cheung, who took up the vice presidency in August, also called for more government funding, saying grant applications took time and returns on investment could be slow.

articles.summary:
Hong Kong refrained from setting overly rigid economic indicators in its first five-year plan to avoid fuelling concerns that it was moving towards a planned economy, according to the city’s constitutional affairs minister.
The current priority should be hitting targets instead of dwelling on accountability mechanisms for potential shortcomings, Secretary for Constitutional and Mainland Affairs Janice Tse Siu-wa said.

articles.summary:
Malaysia’s Anwar Ibrahim is expected to roll out a populist budget on Friday aimed at placating voter concerns over the cost of living and access to essential services, experts say, as the prime minister seeks to shore up support ahead of a general election that could be called as soon as next year.

articles.summary:
The US Air Force has removed its bombers stationed at a US-run military airbase in England used to strike Iran following an investigation into a planned terror attack at the RAF Fairford base.
The bombers were redeployed back to their home bases in the United States, according to a Pentagon official who was not authorised to discuss sensitive military movements and spoke on Sunday on condition of anonymity.

articles.summary:

Netanyahu “has instructed the head of the National Security Council, Shmuel Ben Ezra, to appoint an examiner to conduct a thorough review of all security aspects of foreign civil aviation to Israel”, a statement from the premier’s office said.

articles.title: Brazil heads to run-off between Lula and pro-Trump Senator Flavio Bolsonaro
articles.summary:
Brazil’s presidential election will go to a run-off on October 25 between President Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva and Senator Flavio Bolsonaro, who has promised the Trump administration access to Brazil’s rare earths to cut US reliance on China.
Asked about the vote on Thursday before boarding his helicopter, US President Donald Trump said he was following it “very closely”.

articles.summary:

articles.summary:
A woman suspected of carrying out an attempted robbery with a knife at a Hong Kong shopping centre was arrested after police officers traced her to a flat at a Wong Tai Sin estate on Sunday night.
Police received a report at about 6.50pm that a woman in her forties carrying a knife had travelled from Diamond Hill MTR station towards the nearby Plaza Hollywood mall.

articles.summary:
A march protesting against the imprisonment of former Pakistani prime minister Imran Khan kicked off in northwest Pakistan on Sunday after talks to avoid the demonstration stalled.
Authorities have been preparing for weeks for the possible arrival of demonstrators in Islamabad, with the march planned by supporters of Khan’s Pakistan Tehreek-e-Insaf (PTI) party originally slated for September 27 and then postponed until Sunday.

articles.summary:

A Security Bureau spokesman said that participants took franchised buses or cross-boundary coaches from various districts to reach the crossing and were shown the new port building in groups.

articles.title: Hotstone Yoga closure losses rise to HK$7.8 million as 694 customers file reports
articles.summary:
Losses linked to the abrupt closure of Hotstone Yoga have risen to nearly HK$8 million (US$1 million), with close to 700 reports filed by affected customers in Hong Kong, according to authorities.
The Customs and Excise Department said that as of 6pm on Sunday, it had received 694 reports relating to the yoga chain, involving service contracts worth about HK$7.8 million.

archive.security_status_cs: Prezident Xi Jinping posiluje důraz na vnitřní stabilitu a bezpečnost v předvečer sjezdu strany, zatímco regionální ekonomiku nadále pohání silná globální poptávka po AI a infrastruktuře, jako je nový kanál Pinglu. Zároveň přetrvávají technologická rizika, o čemž svědčí vyšetřování citlivých výzkumníků a přísná opatření vůči dezinformacím.

Meanwhile, technological friction persists, highlighted by heightened scrutiny over researchers and measures against online disinformation.

Čína mezitím zrychluje technologickou soběstačnost skrze otevřený zdrojový kód pro Huawei čipy, zatímco regionální ekonomické reformy a finanční iniciativy v Hongkongu ukazují na snahu o stabilizaci.

China continues its technological advancement under tight regulatory oversight, while Hong Kong benefits from steady foreign capital inflows despite macroeconomic headwinds.

Ekonomický vývoj v regionu je smíšený: zatímco Hongkong hlásí oživení maloobchodních tržeb během svátků, IPO trh nadále oslabuje a technologické restrikce (např. blokování VPN pro AI modely) se zostřují.

Washington mezitím stupňuje technologický a bezpečnostní tlak, včetně jaderných simulací a snah o zajištění alternativních dodávek kritických surovin, jako je wolfram a lithium.
archive.security_status_en: Geopolitical tensions are escalating amid US export controls on AI servers and sanctions evasion schemes routed through Southeast Asia. archive.forecast_en: Over the coming days, markets are expected to react to the uncovered illicit AI technology shipments to China and ongoing diplomatic maneuvers surrounding critical minerals. Attention will also focus on Asian retail data.

archive.forecast_en: Over the coming days, markets are expected to focus on post-holiday consumer activity data in China and the implications of European trade policy on the automotive sector. Attention will also turn to further developments regarding critical raw materials.
